title: What is known about 1RB0LC_0LC0RF_1RD1LC_0RA1LE_---0LD_1LF1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_0LC0RF_1RD1LC_0RA1LE_---0LD_1LF1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and it is a Collatz-type question. Lean proves (kernel) that the machine halts from blank tape exactly when an explicit three-counter map, started at (1, 1, 4), reaches its halting case. The map has survived four refills of its budget; the fifth budget holds about 21479 pairs, far beyond any computation, and whether it survives depends on the parity of a number that behaves like a coin flip.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 43,569 cells have been visited and 38,638 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.618). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Ten macro rules
claims.text: Between two visits of the head (state D) to the left end of the tape, the tape D>0 0 1^a 0 1^b (01)^c becomes the next one of that shape, by one of ten rules, each proved for all values of its parameters; one more rule shows the halt.

claims.title: Halts if and only if the map halts
claims.text: Iterate next from (1, 1, 4) (reached after 138 steps): the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit reaches halt, the case a = 2, c = 0, b odd. The orbit never takes the uncovered case (an invariant).

claims.title: The map agrees with the machine
claims.text: At all 27,727 visits of the head to the left end in the first 4·10<sup>8</sup> steps the tape has the predicted (a, b, c).

claims.title: Four budgets survived, the fifth out of reach
claims.text: The orbit, computed exactly with whole stretches of a ≥ 3 at once, refills its budget at cycles 3, 8, 25 and 2,549, to c = 9, 31, 4,966 and a 1,479-bit number. Spending that budget takes about 2<sup>1478</sup> more rounds.

claims.title: A coin flip per budget
claims.text: Each time the budget runs out, the machine halts if the next even value of a is 2 mod 4 and refills otherwise. If those residues behave like fair coins, the machine halts with probability 1, but at a time beyond the fifth budget, about 2<sup>1478</sup> rounds of a map whose counter grows by half each round.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Equivalent to whether the orbit of (1, 1, 4) under the map ever ends a budget on the wrong parity: a Collatz-type question like Antihydra's, out of reach of current methods.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, and it is a Collatz-type problem. The machine runs a counter that grows by half each round, and pays for its even rounds from a budget; when the budget runs out it either halts or refills it, depending on a parity that behaves like a coin flip. Lean proves that this description is exact.

facts.text: Proved in Lean: the machine is exactly the three-counter map below.
survived; the fifth holds about 2<sup>1479</sup> pairs.
No halt in the C simulator; 43,569 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Three counters on the tape
html: Stop the machine every time the head, in state D, is at the left end of the tape. The tape then always reads

two blocks of 1s, of lengths a and b, followed by c pairs 0 1. In one round the head carries a hole through the first block and comes back: two 1s leave the first block and three join the second. So while a ≥ 3, a round is (a, b, c) → (a − 2, b + 3, c).
When the first block is down to 1 or 2 cells, the second block becomes the new first block, a fresh second block of 3 or 4 cells is written, and pairs are spent:

• a = 1: (1, b, c) → (b + 1, 4, c − 1); one pair spent (none if c = 0, and then the new block has 3 cells);
  • a = 2: (2, b, c) → (b + 6, 4, c − 3); three pairs spent; with only 2 or 1 pairs left they are all spent;
  • a = 2 and c = 0: if b is even the pairs are refilled from the second block, (1, 1, b/2 + 1); if b is odd the head reads a 1 where it needs a 0 and the machine halts.

Starting with first block a, the round sequence ends at a = 1 (a odd) or a = 2 (a even), and the new first block is about 3a/2: exactly 3a/2 + 7 for even a and (3a + 7)/2 for odd a. This is the same 3/2 map as in Antihydra, and even values cost three pairs while odd ones cost one.

Lean proves each of these rules for all values (lean/Rules.lean), and from them that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if this map, started at (1, 1, 4), reaches the halting case (halts_iff in lean/Map.lean).

sections.heading: A budget that runs out
html: The pairs are a budget. Each even value of the counter costs 3 and each odd one costs 1, and the budget only comes back when it is completely spent and the next even value of the counter comes with an even second block, which happens when that value is 0 mod 4. If it is 2 mod 4, the machine halts.

From blank tape the budget has run out four times, and four times it was refilled: at cycle 3 (to 9 pairs), 8 (31), 25 (4,966) and 2,549 (a number of 1,479 bits, about 1.4·10445). Each refill is about half the second block, which by then is enormous, so the next budget lasts about 21478 rounds. No computer will get there.

If the residues mod 4 of the counter are like coin flips, as they appear to be, each budget ends in a halt with probability 1/2, so the machine would halt with probability 1, but only after a time that dwarfs everything here. Proving it either way would mean controlling the parities of a 3/2 map, the same obstacle as for Antihydra and the Collatz problem.
Try the map. Start from any (a, b, c) and step through rounds; each line is one visit of the head to the left end (stretches with a ≥ 3 are taken in one jump).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.618). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 43,569 cells (32,886 left of the start, 10 right), with a density of 1s of 0.887.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Antihydra-like: a 3/2 map on one counter, paid for from a budget of 01 pairs; it halts iff a budget runs out on the wrong parity (survived 4 refills; the 5th budget has 2^1479 pairs).
